ai.description: *Cnemaspis sisparensis* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and dark lateral blotches. Key features include keeled ventral scales and a slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis sisparensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Sispara Day Gecko inhabits high-elevation evergreen shola forests and rocky outcrops in the Nilgiri Hills, typically found at altitudes above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sispara Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis sisparensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sispara Day Gecko is endemic to the high-elevation shola-grasslands of the Nilgiri Hills in the Western Ghats, spanning the states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
